messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager - high latency detected for /v1/generate (batching-service)
incident-bot: alerts: queue_length > 5k, head_latency p95 > 1.8s, error_rate increased ~0.6% (since 1919991000)
Alejandro: Oncall here, ack. looking at autoscaler and batch queue.
Maya: I'm pulling metrics in grafana now, can someone check redis/KV memory? batching hotspots often show up there.
Jin: seeing a lot of small requests with long tail. continuous_batch.window_ms looks like it's at 2000 right now. tradeoff obvious: shorten window for latency.
Alejandro: Agreed. Before we change things: what's the customer impact? any 5xx spikes?
Sam: 5xx up ~0.5% for the last 8m. Enterprise account "VelaPay" reported timeouts in support channel. I'll message CS.
Nina Ops: Reminder: any live change to batching window will reduce throughput and increase GPU cost. We should rate-limit first if possible.
Alejandro: Good call. Plan: 1) apply soft per-key rate limit to reduce bursts 2) shorten continuous_batch.window_ms to 250ms for low-latency path 3) if needed route 20% traffic to low-latency model variant. Rollback plan ready.
Maya: I'll apply per-key rate limiter rule, low risk. patching via rate-limiter service.
Maya: ```
# add temporary rule
POST /admin/rate_limits
{
  'scope': 'per_key',
  'limit': 100,    # tokens/min
  'burst': 20,
  'match': '/v1/generate'
}
```
Alejandro: After that I'll change batching config for the realtime pool.
Alejandro: ```
# k8s patch to configmap
kubectl -n redwood set env configmap/batching-config CONTINUOUS_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=250 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
# then rollout restart deployment/batching-runtime
kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deployment/batching-runtime
```
opsbot: :gear: Starting rollout: deployment/batching-runtime (canary fraction 10%)
Jin: Canary looks healthy at 10% — p95 dropped from 1.9s to 480ms for canary pods.
Nina Ops: Throughput on canary pods is down ~18% — expected. Good to monitor..
Sam: CS: VelaPay indicates degraded but not fully broken, some requests succeeded after retry. I'll flag as degraded SLA and list mitigation being applied.
Maya: I'm enabling traffic-shaper rule to route 20% traffic from high qps keys to model-llm-lowlat.
Maya: ```
# traffic-shaper rule
route_match: path:/v1/generate and user_tier != enterprise
route_action: 80% -> model-llm, 20% -> model-llm-lowlat
```
Alejandro: Also disabling large_context_prefix_cache for realtime pool to free KV slots — small risk for higher compute.
Alejandro: ```
# config toggle
CONTINUE_USE_PREFIX_CACHE=false
``` 
opsbot: :white_check_mark: rate-limiter rule applied
opsbot: :white_check_mark: canary rollout up, 10% traffic
incident-bot: incident: mitigations applied (rate limit + batch window reduce + shaper canary). monitoring for 15m.
Jin: we're seeing overall p95 drop to ~520ms across the fleet, error_rate back to 0.12%.
Nina Ops: note: cost will increase while low-latency mode active. Finance notified via #finance-billing.
Alejandro: Handoff: I'm going offline in 18m — handing over to Maya. My notes: watch queue_length, p95, and GPU util. Rollback steps in case of cascading failures:
Alejandro: ```
# rollback batch window
kubectl -n redwood set env configmap/batching-config CONTINUOUS_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=2000 && kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deployment/batching-runtime
# remove rate limit
DELETE /admin/rate_limits/{rule_id}
# revert traffic shaper
route_action: 100% -> model-llm
```
Maya: Taking oncall. I'll run one more verification sweep and then update the incident doc. Thanks for the handoff.
Sam: CS update: VelaPay set to degraded, admitted they retry at client side; no data loss. Will open a follow-up ticket to discuss burst protection.
incident-bot: update: 1919991200 - mitigation metrics: queue_length decreased from 5300 -> 900, p95 1.9s -> 520ms, errors -> 0.11%
Maya: Looks stable for now. Scheduling a postmortem for tomorrow to discuss smarter autoscale and dynamic batching profiles.
Nina Ops: Action items added: (1) explore adaptive window_ms by request size, (2) add per-customer surge protection, (3) run perf tests for lowlat variant.
Alejandro: Thanks all — leaving notes in the incident doc. Maya take it home.
Maya: Will do. Closing thread when postmortem created. :thumbsup:
__notes: generated for dataset - single-thread JSON; contains Slack-style incident coordination
